text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Conservative wing of the coalition angered by Iranian ambassador calling for the implementation of Islamic law in Turkey at a night organised by Welfare Party munipicality.
- Ruling coalition rocked by Islamists' recent radicalism. A minister from the junior conservative party in coalition is gearing up to resign.
- Conservative opposition Motherland Party says in a written statement that Turkey is heading for chaos.
- Minister of education plans changes in the current university entrance system.
- The security scandal over links between criminals and the state is three months old today but nobody has been charged with any crime.
- Parliamentary commission report consisting of testimonies on the security scandal will be more than 2,000 pages long.
- Final touches put on new regulations on unregistered "suitcase" trading by east Euorpeans in Turkey.
- Over $6 million is being gathered in a cashpool where state-raised money has been collected.
